newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends down but off lows, trade supports.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends down but off lows, trade supports.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed barely weaker and well off the lows after late-session trade buying provided support, dealers said.
Expectations for a strong export number in Thursday's weekly report may have given the market a boost, they added, pegging exports at more than 200,000 bales.
The report will reflect business done during the week ended April 3 and amid talk of sales to China.
May ended 0.15 cent lower at 72.10 cents per lb, having ranged from 72.25 to 70.90, a new contract low. The back months settled 0.27 lower to 0.05 firmer.
Volume was estimated at 17,000 lots compared with Tuesday's official 10,890 lots.
Earlier in the day, speculative liquidation pressured benchmark May to a fresh, life-of-contract low of 70.90 cents, and brisk spread activity contributed to losses.
"The specs are willing to pay whatever it takes to get out of May," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said. "Open interest is huge. They have to start getting out."
Open interest stood at 30,801 lots as of Tuesday's close. The first notice day for May cotton is April 24.
Certificated stocks, meanwhile, continue to pressure the May/July spread. Stocks rose to 220,801 bales as of April 8 compared with 219,842 bales the previous session.
Cotton marketing specialist O.A. Cleveland of Mississippi State Universtiy said players are concerned about burgeoning cotton supplies.

"We continue to have very strong export sales that, to some degree, will mitigate the decline in prices," he said. "But the pressure could take May below 70.00 cents if certificated stocks are still around in July."
The market awaits the U.S. Department of Agriculture's weekly export and sales report on Thursday, and the monthly supply and demand report on Friday.
